Acceptance or verification criterion: During a WAN-only partition with operational edge and LAN, all declared supported local workflows remain available.
No acknowledged local commit is lost in tested application/worker restart cases; durable outbox remains consistent.
A business change and corresponding pending journal intent are committed atomically or both rolled back.
Zero unexpected invalid references or silent lost updates in predefined integrity cases.
100% of predefined forbidden access attempts are rejected across UI and direct API paths.
Protect transport, credentials, privileged logs and stored backups in accordance with selected policies.
Every acknowledged local commit is retrievable by a second authorised client without central access.
For declared deterministic equivalent operations, edge and reference responses/record effects match defined oracles.
100% agreement for the pinned set of reference comparison fixtures; report unsupported semantics separately.
100% of integrity-critical known conflicts detected in seeded tests; report overall precision and recall.
Zero unintended duplicate business objects in the defined repeat/lost-acknowledgement tests.
Each eligible journal operation has a traceable pending, accepted, rejected, uncertain or review-required outcome.
Application/sync restart yields no missing committed operations and restores consistent processing state.
Offline privilege and credential freshness decisions follow documented deny/expiry policy.
Measure p50/p95 latency at fixed 5/10/20-user workloads; candidate p95 under 2 s for selected simple requests, pending feasibility.
Report sustained successful writes/s and reads/s for configured workloads and reference hardware.
Measure time to stable central outcomes after restoration for backlog sizes 100/1000 and report unresolved items.
Measure and publish CPU, memory and disk storage growth under each workload; limits set before acceptance.
Test increasing local client concurrency at 1/5/10/20 sessions and report saturation and errors.
Provide operator-visible health, last successful sync, queue depth, rejection and conflict metrics.
Every conflict decision and privilege-changing operation includes accountable actor, time and outcome.
All integrations use documented pinned-version DHIS2 APIs or supported reuse mechanisms; exceptions logged.
Implementation separated into tested local execution, persistence, journal, sync and administrative components.
Reproduce prototype in documented reference Linux/server environment using versioned deployment steps.
Users can distinguish locally committed from centrally accepted records; errors are actionable.
Use semantic forms, keyboard navigation and readable states in any new administration interfaces.
Repeat test scenarios with fixed seed, reset conditions, version record and uniquely identified runs.
Document time source/time zone and detect unsafe clock drift in test setup.
A verified restoration retains committed records and their pending/accepted reconciliation history.
When disk, DB or credentials prevent durable acceptance, reject explicitly; never report false success.
Synthetic data only for planned university experiments; collect only necessary audit details.
A successful supported local operation makes no blocking central API call on its critical path.
An incompatible metadata change does not silently reinterpret unacknowledged local operations.
Sync worker failures do not crash or block supported local application execution.
Report exact DHIS2 version, metadata fixture, software dependencies, hardware and unsupported cases.
